subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply when an active session transcript is too large or dangerous to open during gateway restart?
rationale: The remaining fix affects persisted user transcripts and unattended gateway availability, so automation should not choose between quarantine, truncation, skip-on-load, reset, or doctor-only repair without maintainer intent.

options.title: Quarantine and Degrade by Default
options.body: Preserve the oversized transcript, skip loading it on restart, mark the session degraded, and keep the gateway available while doctor/manual recovery remains possible.

options.title: Truncate Oldest History Automatically
options.body: Rewrite the active transcript to a bounded tail so the session remains usable, accepting automatic loss of older context.

options.title: Require Manual Doctor Repair
options.body: Fail with a clear recovery path and no automatic rewrite, preserving all data but leaving unattended services down until operator action.

recommendation.title: Quarantine and Degrade by Default
recommendation.body: Preserve the oversized transcript, skip loading it on restart, mark the session degraded, and keep the gateway available while doctor/manual recovery remains possible.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame and recent adjacent commits point to this owner for the active runner/session recovery surface.
